title: POC credits, scaling and legal checkpoints
next_steps: Redwood to send POC credit allocation spreadsheet
SE to propose benchmark script and sample payloads
Customer legal to review pilot T&Cs and return comments by 2025-03-14
action_items: Avery Chen: Share pricing + credits matrix - 2025-03-06
Marco Diaz: Upload benchmark harness & sample prompts to shared folder - 2025-03-07
Priya Raman: Provide 2 representative production prompt sets and expected qps per tier - 2025-03-10
Lisa Tan: Kick off procurement checklist + initial redlines - 2025-03-14
summary: Discovery to align POC commercial guardrails: Bluewave needs a credit structure that supports burst testing, clear SLOs for latency, and legal checkpoints for SOC2 / data residency. Agreed on benchmark targets (99th < 350ms for 2k qps sim) and a 4-week pilot with staged credit release tied to milestone completion.
transcript:
[00:00] Avery Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick roll call — we have Marco from SE and me from AE team. Bluewave team?
[00:08] Priya Raman: Hi, Priya here. Jorge and Lisa on.
[00:12] Jorge Mendez: Hey all.
[00:15] Lisa Tan: Lisa, procurement.
[00:18] Avery Chen: Great. Objective for today: scope the POC from both technical and commercial lenses — success criteria, how many credits you need to run the benchmarks, and what legal checkpoints we need for procurement.
[00:28] Priya Raman: Sounds good. We're mainly worried about two things: can Redwood meet our latency SLOs and how predictable the cost is during spike tests? We have to present an internal business case.
[00:36] Marco Diaz: Totally. From the SE side I'll map workload to model variants and run a small synthetic harness to predict token costs. Two quick q's for you Priya: what's your typical prompt length and expected concurrency for the POC?
[00:47] Priya Raman: Average prompt 120 tokens, sometimes 400 for long form. For the POC phase we want to simulate 200–2,000 QPS across an hour-long soak and a 10-minute stress spike to 5k qps.
[00:58] Marco Diaz: Ok that's helpful. For 120 tokens x 2k qps that's roughly 240k tokens/sec or around 14.4M tokens/minute — sorry, my head math — okay, tokens/minute 14.4M, which is a significant volume. We'll recommend batching profiles and a dedicated slot for the stress run.
[01:17] Jorge Mendez: That math gives us the sense of cost — how do credits work here? We need a cap, and we can't have unexpected overages while legal approves the contract.
[01:24] Avery Chen: Yes. For pilots we typically allocate credits up front in tranches. We'll do an initial tranche to cover baseline benchmark (soak + one stress), then release additional credits once the first milestone — successful 2k qps run with 95th/99th latency targets — is validated. We'll encode the tranche rules in the pilot terms.
[01:40] Lisa Tan: What does 'validated' mean operationally? Who signs off?
[01:44] Marco Diaz: Good callout. We propose sign-off criteria: 1) benchmark harness run by Redwood + customer using the same script; 2) agreed metrics: 95th < 220 ms, 99th < 350 ms for your long-prompt mix; 3) error rate < 0.5% for inference timeouts; 4) artifacts: logs, token-cost CSV, and per-route traces exported to the shared console. When these are present, Avery can release next tranche.
[02:11] Priya Raman: Those numbers look reasonable. 99th < 350 ms is our main stoplight for product.
[02:16] Jorge Mendez: For the legal path, Lisa, what do you need? SOC2 attestation? Data residency notes?
[02:22] Lisa Tan: We'll need SOC2 Type II, at least the SOC2 report and an outline of encryption and KMS options. Also contract language around data retention and deletion on pilot completion. We're also checking if there are any export controls on the data.
[02:33] Avery Chen: We can share SOC2 docs and the security whitepaper. Redwood Private options for VPC/private deployments exist, but for a pilot hosted model we can provide isolated tenancy and contractual KMS controls. I'll attach the security pack and sample pilot T&Cs after the call.
[02:48] Priya Raman: One more: can we throttle or pause the pilot if we hit a cost threshold? We want an automatic kill or alert before spend exceeds budget.
[02:56] Marco Diaz: Yes, the platform supports per-customer spend caps and route-level throttles. For the POC we can configure an automatic hold at 80% of credits used and send an alert to your procurement Slack/channel and to Lisa's email.
[03:10] Lisa Tan: Perfect. That alleviates budget overflow concerns.
[03:14] Avery Chen: On the timeline: you mentioned 4-week pilot. Our recommended structure — week 0: legal and kickoff; week 1: baseline soak at 200 qps and correctness checks; week 2: scale to 2k qps, run latency targets; week 3: stress tests including 5k burst and edge-case prompts + security review and final sign-off. Does that align?
[03:33] Priya Raman: Yes, though we might want two soak days at 2k for production confidence.
[03:37] Marco Diaz: We can add a second soak day within week 2 and adjust tranche release timing accordingly. That would mean initial tranche covers week 1 and first 2k soak; second tranche releases after second 2k soak and verified latency.
[03:51] Jorge Mendez: How do we instrument real production traffic? We want to make sure synthetic tests mimic our fanout patterns and conversation lengths.
[03:58] Marco Diaz: We'll ask for two representative prompt sets: one for short-turn Q&A and one for long-form summarization. We'll parameterize the harness to reproduce inter-arrival times and token distributions. Also we can replay sanitized logs if you provide them.
[04:13] Priya Raman: We'll sanitize and provide a subset. Expect that by 2025-03-10.
[04:18] Avery Chen: Great. On costing: I want to be transparent — the initial estimate for the 4-week pilot with the described runs (soak + 2x 2k soaks + 5k stress) is X credits, we'll quantify in spreadsheet. Credits are consumed per-token but we'll show a per-run estimated spend.
[04:34] Jorge Mendez: Can you give a ballpark now?
[04:36] Marco Diaz: Very rough: assuming medium-sized model variant and 120 tokens avg, the 2k soak hour is roughly 14.4M tokens/minute earlier we mis-spoke — to clarify, it's 14.4M tokens per minute is incorrect, it's 240k tokens per second => 14.4M tokens per minute, yes that math stands, though we should double-check; but in practice the platform discounts via batching efficiency so the effective credit burn will be lower. We'll provide modeled estimates in the spreadsheet.
[05:01] Priya Raman: Ok our finance will need that line itemized per run.
[05:06] Avery Chen: We'll send an itemized credits table that maps to milestone tranches. Also include a reserve bucket for exploratory testing (10% of total) that requires separate approval to unlock.
[05:16] Lisa Tan: For contract terms: we need a limited pilot agreement (no indemnities beyond standard), NDA for data exchange, and a clear off-ramp: delete data after 30 days unless we opt into contract.
[05:26] Avery Chen: Redwood's standard pilot T&Cs include data deletion within 30 days and no surprise indemnities. We'll send sample language. If Bluewave needs a corporate agreement later, we can map usage into a reserved capacity quote.
[05:36] Jorge Mendez: Regarding SLA — we expect an uptime commitment for any dedicated slot used during the POC. What can you guarantee for hosted pilot?
[05:43] Marco Diaz: For pilots we don't usually offer enterprise SLA by default on hosted plans, but for Dedicated or Dedicated-like pilot slots we can offer an uptime target of 99.5% for the test windows and a latency objective in the milestone. It requires a short addendum; we'll include it as an optional clause.
[05:59] Priya Raman: That's reasonable. Can you also capture regional placement? We want EU region for some datasets.
[06:05] Avery Chen: Yes, region placement is configurable. For data residency needs we can provision EU-hosted inference for the pilot. That may affect scheduling and capacity but it's doable.
[06:14] Lisa Tan: On insurance and data processing: we need to see Redwood's DPA and proof of cyber insurance up to a threshold.
[06:21] Avery Chen: We'll include DPA and insurance certificate in the security pack.
[06:25] Marco Diaz: Back to the technicals — for the benchmark script, we'll instrument the following metrics: per-request latency, token counts per request, batching efficiency, GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate, error types. That will help explain variability in 99th latencies.
[06:40] Priya Raman: KV cache hit rate — we use lots of repeated prefixes so that may help.
[06:44] Marco Diaz: Good — in that case we'll enable prefix caching and measure delta vs cold runs. It can materially reduce both latency and cost.
[06:52] Jorge Mendez: Who runs the benchmark? We need both teams to run it to confirm reproducibility.
[06:58] Marco Diaz: Agreed. Redwood runs the first pass in our staging with your script; then Priya's team runs it from Bluewave side against the same endpoint. We'll reconcile logs.
[07:07] Priya Raman: We'll need a hand getting the replay harness configured. Marco, can you do a quick walkthrough?
[07:11] Marco Diaz: Yep, I'll document steps and share a recording. Expect that by 2025-03-07.
[07:18] Lisa Tan: Payment terms for credits — do we prepay for all credits or can we do a refundable escrow until legal signs off?
[07:24] Avery Chen: We can do a net-30 invoice against used credits for qualified enterprise pilots, or prepay credits for self-serve. For this pilot Bluewave qualifies for invoiced usage under existing sales process; invoice cadence can be aligned to tranche releases. Procurement can mark milestones as triggers for invoice issuance.
[07:39] Jorge Mendez: So years net-30, but risk of overuse still exists. The automatic hold at 80% is key.
[07:45] Avery Chen: We'll add a hard stop that prevents new calls once 100% of allocated credits for the tranche are consumed unless procurement authorizes an unlock.
[07:53] Priya Raman: Good. Let's talk about success criteria again — aside from latency and error rate, we want a qualitative assessment: model output quality on our eval set (f1 or human rated).
[08:03] Marco Diaz: We'll include a small eval harness for quality checks. Ideally run a blind A/B between model variant and your baseline; we can compute automatic metrics and provide human review samples.
[08:12] Priya Raman: We'll budget for 20 human reviews per model variant during the POC.
[08:17] Avery Chen: Noted. On procurement path: next steps I propose — Redwood sends pilot T&Cs + security pack + credit spreadsheet by 2025-03-06; Customer provides prompt sets and sanitized logs by 2025-03-10; SE delivers benchmark harness + run plan by 2025-03-07; legal returns initial redlines by 2025-03-14. After legal signoff we target pilot start w/c 2025-03-17.
[08:40] Lisa Tan: That timeline works, Lisa will try to get redlines earlier if possible.
[08:44] Jorge Mendez: One operational nuance — we need to ensure the pilot doesn't require data egress we can't permit. Can Redwood guarantee encrypted in-transit and at-rest for pilot data?
[08:54] Marco Diaz: Yes, TLS in transit and AES-256 at rest. For KMS we can integrate with your key if we do Private or dedicated. For hosted pilot we provide our managed KMS but will add contractual controls.
[09:06] Priya Raman: Anything else on security?
[09:08] Lisa Tan: pen test report if available, and an escalation contact for incidents during pilot runs.
[09:14] Avery Chen: We'll provide contact and incident response summary.
[09:18] Marco Diaz: Quick note on observability: we can give you access to the Redwood Console for the POC with token-level cost dashboards and per-route tracing. That will make sign-off easier.
[09:28] Priya Raman: Please do.
[09:30] Avery Chen: OK to recap and capture the concrete milestone/tranche mapping so procurement has something to review?
[09:36] Jorge Mendez: Yes let's do that.
[09:38] Marco Diaz: Milestone 0: Kickoff & legal clearance — initial tranche (cover baseline soak + 1st 2k run).
[09:44] Marco Diaz: Milestone 1: 2k soak day 1 pass — monitoring artifacts uploaded (logs, traces) — release tranche 2 for second 2k soak + stress testing.
[09:53] Marco Diaz: Milestone 2: 2k soak day 2 and 5k stress pass + quality eval (human reviews) — final tranche released and pilot closeout report prepared.
[10:03] Priya Raman: If any milestone fails we'll do a remediation window of 3 business days and re-run the test.
[10:10] Avery Chen: Sounds fair. We'll reflect the remediation window in the pilot T&Cs.
[10:15] Lisa Tan: Please include a clause for escrow of data deletion confirmation at pilot end.
[10:21] Avery Chen: Yes.
[10:22] Jorge Mendez: Great, I think we have coverage. A couple micro items — do you provide a stub SOW mapping credits to resource reservations?
[10:29] Avery Chen: Yes, we'll attach a stub SOW outlining reserved GPU capacity for the stress windows and credit-to-GPU mapping.
[10:34] Marco Diaz: Also note that if we hit unexpected contention in the EU region we might suggest a cross-region fallback for the stress run and mark it as optional in the harness.
[10:44] Priya Raman: Ok we'll take that under advisement.
[10:46] Lisa Tan: For procurement acceptance, can you provide a single PDF with T&Cs, DPA, SOC2, insurance cert, and the credit spreadsheet? Makes reviews easier.
[10:55] Avery Chen: Absolutely — one packet. We'll aim to deliver by 2025-03-06.
[10:59] Marco Diaz: I'll also include a short how-to for the harness and a recorded walkthrough.
[11:03] Priya Raman: Thanks both. One last question — what's the path to convert the pilot into reserved capacity if we want predictability after pilot?
[11:11] Avery Chen: We map pilot metrics into a reserved capacity proposal. If you hit performance and quality thresholds we'll fast-track a Dedicated quote — usually 4–6 week contracting for Dedicated with capacity planning. We'll include a conversion playbook in the packet.
[11:23] Jorge Mendez: Great.
[11:25] Avery Chen: Ok, I'll summarize in the follow-up email and attach docs. Any final points?
[11:29] Lisa Tan: No, just watch the credit release rules carefully.
[11:33] Priya Raman: We'll provide prompt sets by 2025-03-10.
[11:36] Avery Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll circle back with the packet and schedule the harness walkthrough for 2025-03-07.
[11:43] Jorge Mendez: Thanks all.
[11:45] [call ends]
